headline: She herself wants to return, she'll say extradite me, I see no complications: Zahed Ur Rahman

members.title: She herself wants to return, she'll say extradite me, I see no complications: Zahed Ur Rahman
members.lead: Since ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who is currently in India, wants to return to the country herself, the government foresees no complications under extradition law, Information and Broadcasting Adviser to the prime minister, Zahed Ur Rahman, has said. The information adviser made these remarks today, Tuesday in response to journalists' questions at a regular briefing held at the Secretariat to report on government activities. .If Sheikh Hasina wants to return, govt will act under extradition treaty. Zahed Ur Rahman said, “We want to extradite her. We want to bring her back... Now, she wants to return herself. That means she does not even need to go to the court. She will simply say 'extradite me'... Therefore, regarding the legal process or legal complexities being talked about concerning extradition, I, at least, see none.” The information adviser remarked that the government wants the convicted accused extradited, and the Indian government must allow this to happen, adding that Indian government should have no reason for concern at this point. He stated, “Because the person who is to be extradited wants to come back herself. So, we no longer believe there is any legal issue.” .Sheikh Hasina's new passport: Delhi receives email, forwards it to Dhaka. A Reuters report on Monday revealed that ousted Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina has applied for a new passport and National Identity Card (NID) to return home. She submitted the application to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, India, according to a letter obtained by Reuters. According to Reuters, this is the first such application Sheikh Hasina has made since fleeing to India on 5 August 2024 amid student-led mass protests. This step is being viewed as the clearest indication yet of her plan to return to Bangladesh, which she intends to do this coming December. members.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh after two years in exile
members.lead: Hasina fled to India in 2024 after mass uprising. She faces death penalty upon return Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister of Bangladesh applied for a fresh passport this week. Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She fled over the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi. Continue reading...

members.title: It's not that AL cannot hold 'other forms of meetings and rallies': Information Adviser
members.lead: Although the political activities of the Awami League are banned, the Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman does not see any obstacle to their members holding other types of meetings and gatherings. However, he commented that conducting activities under the Awami League banner would be regarded as a legal violation. Today, Tuesday, in response to a question from journalists at the regular press conference organised to present information on the government's current activities, Prime Minister's Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman made these remarks. . A video circulating on social media shows Ranjit Sarkar, a former Member of Parliament for Sunamganj-1 constituency and member of the banned Awami League, entering Bangladesh through the border and holding a meeting in his constituency. This has sparked discussions on social media. When a journalist asked about this matter at the press conference, the Prime Minister's advisor replied that the Awami League's programme is banned. What an individual from the Awami League has done, whether he has conducted any party programmes or meetings, is crucial. Whether the Awami League will be banned or not is being judged by the International Criminal Tribunal (ICT). Until then, the activities of the party are banned through amendments to the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2009. Therefore, Awami League members cannot hold any party meetings or processions. However, an individual affiliated with the Awami League, if they do not have any criminal charges, are not in jail, or are out on bail, can organise other types of meetings or gatherings. . The advisor stated, "Now, I'm not sure if the meeting (of Ranjit Sarkar) was an Awami League programme? Was it under the Awami League banner?" In response, the journalist mentioned that the meeting was indeed held with a banner and a pandal. members.title: No alternative to carrying out Sheikh Hasina’s death sentence: Chief Prosecutor
members.lead: Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal, Md Aminul Islam, said that there is no alternative to enforcing the death sentences once Sheikh Hasina returns to the country. He made this statement the day after the news broke about the ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina applying for a passport to return to the country. During a briefing at the premises of the International Crimes Tribunal on Tuesday, Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam stated that the tribunal law specifies that appeals will not be accepted 30 days after the verdict is announced. Currently, there is no alternative but to enforce the verdict concerning Sheikh Hasina. On 17 November of the previous year, International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced Sheikh Hasina and her government's Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan to death in a case related to crimes against humanity during a mass uprising. Another accused in the case, former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, was sentenced to five years as a state witness. . Fifty-seven days after the verdict announcement, the full judgment of the case was made public on 13 January. The law provides for appeals to be filed within 30 days of publishing the full verdict. It is stated in the judgment that appeals will not be accepted after 30 days. Sheikh Hasina, who fled to India after being ousted in the 2024 coup, has been at large since the trial began. She expressed in an international media interview her intent to return to the country at any cost in December. Renewed discussions on the issue have arisen following the recent news about her passport and national identity card applications. In today's briefing, journalists inquired whether Sheikh Hasina would have the chance for a legal fight upon returning to Bangladesh. In response, Aminul Islam stated, "Whether she gets a legal opportunity or not; what process she will follow to avail herself of a legal opportunity or not; . . . if she is found in Bangladesh, this will be settled…
